title: About two billion
hookLine: a number too big to picture, and the prayer rows behind it

lines: A WAVE OF PRAYER AROUND THE EARTH.
cards: Dawn is moving across the earth right now, a thin gray line sliding west. Wherever it passes, somebody's alarm goes off, somebody washes in cold water, somebody unrolls a mat and stands to pray the dawn prayer.
In Jakarta it happened hours ago. In Dhaka a little later. Then Karachi, then Cairo, then on toward the Atlantic and across it.
As the earth turns, the call to prayer moves with it, like a wave that never quite reaches the shore. Today: about two billion.

teach.b: The title is an estimate, and so is today's line. Researchers who study populations put the number of Muslims in the world at about two billion, roughly a quarter of humanity.
Counts differ, and no census can see into anyone's heart, so hold the number loosely. What matters more is what it's made of. Two billion is not a crowd.

It's one person, then another, then another: a rice farmer in Java, a shopkeeper in Dakar, a midwife in Kazan, a student in Sarajevo, each with their own family, their own questions, their own way of keeping the faith.
They speak a great range of languages. They follow different schools of law and different customs. They argue.
Still, at the times of prayer they turn the same way, toward the Ka'ba in Mecca, and say the same opening chapter in the same Arabic.
The Qur'an speaks to that scattered unity: "And each one hath a goal toward which he turneth; so vie with one another in good works. Wheresoever ye may be, Allah will bring you all together."

These last weeks walked through the modern centuries: colonial rule, the last Mughal, the reformers, Iqbal, the caliphate's end, Partition, independence, enslaved Africans, Britain and America, radio, women scholars, and pain.
That whole story ends here, in one huge number made of single faces.

how: Muslims around the world pray at set times through the day, facing the Ka'ba in Mecca, so the times of prayer move across the globe with the sun.

games.q: it's dawn in Jakarta, and still night in Casablanca. when does Casablanca pray the dawn prayer?
o: at the same moment as Jakarta.
games.why: the prayer follows the sun, so the dawn prayer moves west across the earth like a wave.

practice: Start with one prayer row you can see clearly, a mosque you know or one from a photo, then let it widen: a rooftop in Cairo, a school gym in Toronto, a ship's deck, a refugee camp, one person praying alone in an office stairwell.
Don't count them; let them come one at a time, all turned toward the same center. If you pray, you can join them in your own way.

wordCard.voice: Ka'ba, the house in Mecca that roughly two billion Muslims worldwide turn toward at every prayer. Today's word, and the end of the modern centuries.

carryVoice: Your line: a quarter of humanity. Behind the number, a name, a kitchen, a morning. I'll be here tomorrow.
